correctness.rationale: The left characteristic polynomial has opposite signs at 0 and 1, with positive product and a second root above 1. On the right q_R(-1)<0, q_R(0)<0 and q_R(1)>0 under the stated strict assumptions; thus the roots lie below -1 and in (0,1). Independently expanding H(Fp)-lambda H(p) gives (lambda tau_i-delta_i-lambda^2)x, with the constant canceled by lambda/(1-lambda). The right coefficient is zero, and the left is kappa=(lambda-s_L)(u_L-lambda), including zero at coincidence. Iteration back m steps bounds the omitted affine height by lambda^m times a fixed constant; the forcing sum is absolutely convergent on each bounded complete orbit. Surjectivity F(K)=K allows a full history in K even without invertibility, and 0<=(-x)_+<=R_K makes the resulting interval one-sided. The exact distance uses the normal (lambda,1). The admissible fixed point x_L=1/(1-tau_L+delta_L)<0 gives constant forcing R_K=-x_L on its singleton, so the entire bound is attained for each nonzero mismatch; for kappa=0 the strip collapses. Integration against any compactly supported invariant probability gives the asserted stationary balance. Verified directly on the formulas; the frozen rational spots are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: The result quantifies a natural loss of an invariant line when previously shared stable eigenvalues separate. It confines every compact two-sided invariant set on the same predicted side, with an explicit scale tied to left excursions and a constant saturated by a fixed point. It provides a nontrivial constraint on recurrent sets and invariant measures without requiring a surviving invariant segment. It does not establish attractor persistence or an absolute bound independent of excursion size.
